To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• the model of interpreted systems is geometric in a way analogous to the geometry of groupoids, • the model of S 5 n is geometric in a manner analogous to the geometry groupoids, • there is a notion of ‘path’ that can be applied to interpreted systems, and • the notion of ‘path in S 5 n models’ is similar to the notion of run in MASs.
interpreted systems and Kripke models for S 5 n have a natural homotopy structure and that this structure is related to the homotopy structure of groupoid algebras.

• the geometric structure of a MAS is closely related to the combinatorial structure of the Kripke models for S 5 n ; • the geometric structure can be used to analyse the MAS, and • the geometric structure is closely related to homotopy theory

the following questions: 1. How can we use geometric ideas to understand the behaviour of MASs?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a rich geometric structure to MASs and the logic S 4 n (and S 5 n ), which is not yet fully understood, but is worth further investigation.
the geometric/homology theory of groupoids is a rich source of concepts that can be applied in the study of MASs and epistemic logics.

the geometry of interpreted systems, S 5 n models, and MASs are closely related and that the geometric/homological analysis of the former two is a fruitful approach to the study of MASs, and vice versa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to develop the notion of a ‘geometric’ epistemic logic, in which the Kripke semantics is replaced by a geometric one.
we can see how to use the geometric/homological structure of groupoids to analyse the geometry of the MAS and its Kripke models.

the geometric analysis of the Kripke models for the epistemic logic S 5n, is a rich and interesting subject in its own right, which may yield new insights into the nature of MASs.
